note: A laid-out primitive campground on the point where Tavern Creek meets the Osage River: two gravel loops with about twenty gravel back-in spurs under scattered big trees, a privy and a boat ramp. The spurs on the north side of the upper loop back toward Tavern Creek's wide mouth across mown grass; the Osage itself is behind a belt of bank timber on the west side. Spur length is not published. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Individual Campsites' - a real two-loop gravel campground (~20 spurs on imagery) with a privy beside the ramp, not a lot; free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Pin fine. Phone matches. Waterfront lead UP (north spurs ~15-25 m from Tavern Creek's ~40 m-wide mouth).
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - does not arise): the area page says 'This area offers access to the Osage river. There is a boat ramp and primitive camping is allowed', lists 'Camping: Individual Campsites', and captions a photo 'The Osage-Tavern Access provides individual camping sites and a disabled-accessible privy.' GIS layer 27 has three 'Primitive Camping Area' points (OBJECTIDs 68-70) on the loops. Leaf-off imagery shows two gravel loop roads with about 20-22 separate gravel back-in spurs (my count on a 0.29 m/px frame, not an MDC figure), a privy, and the ramp lot at the north-west corner. Spurs measure roughly 10-15 m; a 23-ft rig fits. Reached by Hoecker Road from the south-east; no ford on that approach (a low bridge/slab over Tavern Creek north-east of the campground is on a different road and is not needed from St. Elizabeth). The page links no map PDF or brochure (the usual 6102map.pdf URL is 404), so there is no map symbol to check.

WATERFRONT LEAD (stored not waterfront; not changed by this result): the campground sits on the point between Tavern Creek (north) and the Osage River (west). On the 0.14 m/px leaf-off frame, five or six spurs on the north side of the upper loop run toward Tavern Creek with their ends ~15-25 m from the water; the ground between is mown grass under scattered mature trees with a single line of bank trees, and no road lies between those spurs and the creek. The creek mouth there is ~40 m of open water (backwater of the Osage), which by the 30 m size rule reads as riverfront rather than creekside. The western spurs are ~45 m from the Osage behind a continuous belt of bank timber (no open apron). What imagery can't show is the bank height. On this read the north spurs earn at least riverview and probably riverfront; no official site photo of the water from a pad was found, so it is offered as a re-audit lead, not a finding.
